subject.title: fix embedded compaction hook reset API

question: Should after-compaction hooks permanently receive a public current-session reset API, and if so should the contract be only resetSession(reason?) or also retain the explicit-session-key compatibility overload?
rationale: This changes the third-party plugin contract and session lifecycle authority; repository policy and current source cannot determine whether compatibility with an externally deployed, unshipped call shape is worth permanently expanding the API.

options.title: Ship the narrow API
options.body: Expose only resetSession(reason?) on successful resettable after-compaction contexts, remove the explicit-key overload, and require complete owner-boundary coverage and live proof.

options.title: Keep the compatibility overload
options.body: Retain explicit-key calls only with maintainer-approved documentation, focused compatibility tests, and a named deprecation or permanence decision.

options.title: Do not add the hook API
options.body: Keep session reset authority outside plugin hooks and close or redesign this branch around an existing owner-controlled lifecycle surface.

recommendation.title: Ship the narrow API
recommendation.body: Expose only resetSession(reason?) on successful resettable after-compaction contexts, remove the explicit-key overload, and require complete owner-boundary coverage and live proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history signal is ownership of the centralized plugin hook contract surface affected by this decision.
